narrative.overview:
Actual particle trails and laser fields surround physical engineering artifacts. Warm, wide HTML identity holds the composition while gold and cyan diffraction move across a dark foil card. The owner's pinned ThreeUI references and rejection of the optical-workbench translation establish this replacement world.

The interface keeps project truth readable around the rendered material. HTML owns names, navigation, actions, provenance and explanation; the original Community fields provide atmosphere and a custom Three.js card provides inspection. The owner removed the lower DARVS, USMHACS and RANGraph illustration panels; those sections now lead with project text and native links. Technical instruments continue the dark glass, metal edge and semantic signal vocabulary.

Owner refinement: the hero is personal identity only; its named project dock is retired. Entry waits for Scan on a full home refresh, with compact/preference/failure alternatives. USMHACS is the copied V1 component with local palette substitutions. See docs/V1-DETAILS.md for source fidelity and current verification limits.

Latest owner entry refinement: remove status/bar/stage clutter; closely frame the supplied interactive face; use a condensed Scan to enter heading, Authenticate your identity subtitle and corner DARVS System Overview link. Morph its points into gold/cyan ribbons and open an aperture onto the prepared hero over a 6.9-second sequence. Face disposal ends the bounded renderer overlap. See docs/ENTRY-MOTION.md for controls and current visual-verification limits.
keyCharacteristics: Full-scale official particle and laser fields behind readable HTML.
Custom gold/cyan foil, physical card edges and a shader-lit native action.
Source-backed architecture, meaningful static views and native controls.
Bounded inspection, explicit motion preferences and precise reference attribution.

rules.name: The Signal Meaning Rule
rules.body: Cyan marks interaction or signal; fault red belongs to a demonstrated failure state, and gold carries material warmth and selected home-system emphasis.

rules.name: The HTML Identity Rule
rules.body: Names, headings, control labels and project truth stay in HTML; rendered card printing supplements them.

rules.name: The Material Provenance Rule
rules.body: Name direct upstream effects precisely and distinguish them from custom studies; an inspired material treatment does not make it the referenced component.

dos: **Do** retain the actual reference fields, warm HTML identity and gold/cyan foil relationship.
**Do** distinguish decorative atmosphere from source-backed project data.
**Do** retain native actions, visible focus, bounded keyboard inspection and mobile vertical scrolling.
**Do** use system-specific static overviews, keep Pause/Resume available independently of the card, and gate reverse/reset on card availability.
**Do** unmount decorative frames when paused, hidden, offscreen or reduced motion is requested.
**Do** keep exact upstream attribution and custom-study boundaries adjacent to the design record.
donts: **Don't** replace the pinned reference materials with the rejected optical-workbench translation.
**Don't** call the custom card Ashen One source or the face a Cortexa Pro component.
**Don't** claim a zero-speed control reliably pauses every upstream renderer.
**Don't** invent telemetry, benchmarks, publications or wireless relationships.
**Don't** present schematic geometry as a measured hardware prototype or running model inference.
**Don't** leave the temporary face in the persistent home composition.
